section_text: General — introduction and adoption of Part A of the ISPS Code as mandatory under SOLAS chapter XI-2.
Definitions — terms used in Part A (Convention, regulation, chapter, security level, ship/port interface, etc.).
Application — applies to ships engaged on international voyages (passenger ships, cargo ships >=500 GT, MODUs) and port facilities serving them.
Responsibilities of Contracting Governments — setting security levels and providing guidance to ships and port facilities.
Declaration of Security — requirements for completing a Declaration of Security between ship and port facility / ship and ship.
Obligations of the Company — ensuring the master has information to establish security and the SSP is provided.
Ship security — ships shall act upon the security levels set by Contracting Governments.
Ship security assessment — an essential and integral part of developing and updating the Ship Security Plan.
Ship security plan — each ship shall carry an approved Ship Security Plan addressing the security levels.
Records — records of activities addressed in the Ship Security Plan shall be kept on board.
Company security officer — the Company shall designate a Company Security Officer.
Ship security officer — a Ship Security Officer shall be designated on each ship.
Training, drills and exercises on ship security — CSO and shore personnel, SSO and shipboard personnel.
Port facility security — port facilities shall act upon the security levels set within whose territory it is located.
Port facility security assessment — an essential and integral part of developing and updating the Port Facility Security Plan.
Port facility security plan — a Port Facility Security Plan shall be developed and maintained for each port facility.
Port facility security officer — a Port Facility Security Officer shall be designated for each port facility.
Training, drills and exercises on port facility security — PFSO and port facility personnel.
Verification and certification for ships — initial, renewal, intermediate and additional verifications.
Verifications — each ship shall be subject to initial, renewal, and at least one intermediate verification of its security system.
Issue or endorsement of the International Ship Security Certificate — issued after initial or renewal verification.
Duration and validity of the certificate — the ISSC shall be issued for a period not exceeding five years.
Interim certification — an Interim International Ship Security Certificate may be issued.
